segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God; believe also in me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In my Father’s house there are many dwelling places. If there were not, I would have told you; for I am going to prepare a place for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And where I am going, you know the way.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thomas said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you had known me, you would have known my Father as well. From now on you do know him, and you have seen him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, show us the Father, and that is enough for us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have I been with you all this time, Philip, and you have not come to know me? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I say to you I do not speak on my own; but the Father, remaining in me, does his works.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or if not, believe because of the works themselves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whatever you ask in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you ask me for anything in my name, I will do it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you love me, you will keep my commandments.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, because he remains with you and will be in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: A little while longer and the world will see me no more, but you will see me; because I live, you also will live.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, that is the one who loves me. And the one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I too will love that person and reveal myself to them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Judas (not Iscariot) said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, what has happened, that you are going to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If anyone loves me, they will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our dwelling with them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine but the Father’s who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you everything and remind you of everything I have said to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Peace I leave with you; my own peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You heard me say to you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I am.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of the world is coming. He has no claim on me,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but so that the world may know that I love the Father, I do just as the Father has commanded me. Get up; let us go from here.”

notes.phrase: Believe in God; believe also in me.
notes.traditional: ye believe in God, believe also in me
notes.note: The Greek verb form used twice here can be either a statement ('you believe') or a command ('believe'). Both are taken as commands here, which suits the opening 'Do not let your hearts be troubled'. The older tradition took the first as a statement and the second as a command, and that remains possible. The verb also carries the sense 'trust'.

The word means a place where one stays or lives. In this Gospel it echoes the verb 'remain' that runs through these chapters. 'Mansions' once meant simply 'lodgings' but now suggests grand houses, which the Greek does not. The same word returns in verse 23, where the Father and the Son 'make our dwelling' with the one who loves Jesus.

notes.phrase: I would have told you; for I am going
notes.traditional: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you
notes.note: The Greek can be punctuated in more than one way. It may also be read as a question: 'If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?' Several modern translations take it that way. The rendering here follows the punctuation of the Greek edition translated, taking the connecting word as 'for' rather than 'that'.

notes.phrase: If you had known me, you would have known my Father as well.
notes.traditional: If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also
notes.note: Manuscripts differ here. Some early witnesses read 'If you have come to know me, you will know my Father also', which makes the sentence a promise rather than a mild reproach. The edition translated here adopts the reproach, which fits the question put to Philip in verse 9. Editors remain divided.

notes.phrase: If you ask me for anything
notes.traditional: If ye shall ask any thing in my name
notes.note: Many manuscripts lack the word 'me', and a few omit the whole verse. The reading with 'me' has strong early support. It may have been dropped because asking Jesus 'in my name' seemed awkward, or to match 16:23.

Many manuscripts have a command here ('keep my commandments'), and the King James tradition follows them. The edition translated here reads a future, 'you will keep', which makes obedience the outcome of love rather than a demand. The two forms differ by only a letter or two in Greek.

In Greek usage of the period the word describes someone called in to speak or act on another's behalf, and 1 John 2:1 uses it of Jesus in exactly that sense. 'Comforter' comes from older English, where it meant 'strengthener', and now suggests consolation only. Current translations are divided between 'Advocate', 'Helper' and 'Counselor'. 'Another' implies that Jesus himself has been the first.

Judas was a very common name. This is a second disciple of that name, probably the 'Judas of James' in Luke's lists of the Twelve (Luke 6:16; Acts 1:13), and often identified with Thaddaeus in Matthew and Mark. Judas Iscariot has already left the meal (13:30).

notes.phrase: He has no claim on me
notes.note: The Greek is literally 'in me he has nothing'. This is generally understood as an idiom, probably reflecting a Semitic legal expression, for having no claim against or hold over someone. Modern versions vary between 'no claim on me', 'no power over me' and 'no hold over me'. The literal wording is now obscure in English.

notes.phrase: but so that the world may know that I love the Father, I do just as the Father has commanded me
notes.traditional: But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do
notes.note: The Greek sentence is compressed and can be construed in more than one way. Alternatively, a main clause is to be supplied: '(this is happening) so that the world may know that I love the Father and that I do just as the Father commanded me.' On either reading the point is that Jesus goes to his death out of obedience, not because the ruler of the world has power over him.

notes.phrase: Get up; let us go from here.
notes.note: Jesus appears to end the meal here, yet the discourse continues for three more chapters, and the group crosses the Kidron valley only at 18:1. Some scholars think chapters 15 to 17 were spoken on the way. Others think they were spoken while the group lingered. Many hold that the Gospel combines more than one version of the farewell discourse. The question is unresolved.
